title: Joshua Chapter 23 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 23 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 23 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 23.

questions.question: What was the condition of Joshua when he spoke to all Israel in chapter 23?
options: He was old and stricken in age
questions.correctAnswer: He was old and stricken in age
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:1 states that Joshua waxed old and stricken in age, and verse 2 repeats he said, 'I am old and stricken in age.'

questions.question: Who did Joshua call for when he gathered the people in chapter 23?
options: All Israel, their elders, heads, judges, and officers
questions.correctAnswer: All Israel, their elders, heads, judges, and officers
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:2 says Joshua called for all Israel, their elders, heads, judges, and officers.

questions.question: According to Joshua 23:3, who fought for Israel against their enemies?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD your God
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:3 says the LORD your God is he that hath fought for you.

questions.question: By what means did Joshua divide the remaining nations for the tribes of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: By lot
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:4 states Joshua divided the nations by lot as an inheritance for the tribes.

questions.question: To which geographical boundary does Joshua refer when describing the inheritance?
options: From the Jordan to the Dead Sea eastward
From the Jordan to the great sea westward
From the Red Sea to the Mediterranean Sea
questions.correctAnswer: From the Jordan to the great sea westward
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:4 mentions the inheritance extends from Jordan to the great sea westward.

questions.question: What does the LORD your God promise to do to the nations remaining in the land?
options: Drive them from out of your sight
Allow them to live among Israel
Give their land to other peoples
questions.correctAnswer: Drive them from out of your sight
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:5 says the LORD will expel them and drive them from before you.

questions.question: What command does Joshua give regarding the book of the law of Moses?
options: To read it once a year
To keep and do all that is written in it
To ignore it after the conquest
questions.correctAnswer: To keep and do all that is written in it
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:6 commands to be courageous to keep and do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses.

questions.question: What warning does Joshua give about turning aside from the law of Moses?
options: Do not turn aside to the right hand or to the left
Turn to the right hand only
Turn to the left hand only
questions.correctAnswer: Do not turn aside to the right hand or to the left
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:6 clearly warns not to turn aside to the right hand or to the left from the law.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua reminded Israel that the LORD had given them rest from all their enemies around about.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:1 states that the LORD had given rest unto Israel from all their enemies round about.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua called only the elders of Israel when he gave his final instructions.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:2 mentions he called all Israel, their elders, heads, judges, and officers, not just the elders.

questions.question: What does Joshua say you have seen concerning what the LORD your God has done?
options: That the LORD has abandoned you
That the LORD has fought for you against all these nations
That the LORD has punished Israel
That the LORD has remained silent
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD has fought for you against all these nations
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:3 says you have seen what the LORD your God hath done unto all these nations because He has fought for you.

questions.question: What does Joshua urge the people to be in keeping the law of Moses?
questions.correctAnswer: Very courageous
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:6 commands the people to be very courageous to keep and do all that is written in the law of Moses.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua says the LORD your God will allow the remaining nations to continue living among Israel without consequence.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:5 promises the LORD will expel and drive out the remaining nations from before you.

questions.question: Which of the following comes FIRST in Joshua 23?
options: Joshua warns against marrying the remaining nations
Joshua calls for all Israel and their leaders
Joshua reminds that the LORD fought for Israel
Joshua commands courage to keep the law
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua calls for all Israel and their leaders
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:2 occurs before the other instructions and warnings mentioned later in the chapter.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua reminds the people that the land they possess was promised by the LORD their God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:5 clearly states that the land possession is as the LORD your God hath promised unto you.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 23 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 23 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Joshua 23:7, what are the Israelites commanded NOT to do regarding the nations remaining among them?
options: Make mention of the name of their gods and serve them
Form alliances with them for battle
Invite them to celebrate Israelite festivals
questions.correctAnswer: Make mention of the name of their gods and serve them
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:7 explicitly commands the Israelites not to come among these nations, not to make mention of the name of their gods, serve them, or bow to them. This is reinforced by the call in Joshua 23:8 to cleave unto the LORD.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Joshua 23:8 for the Israelites to cleave unto the LORD their God?
options: Because the LORD had given them many possessions
As they have done unto this day
To avoid war with other nations
questions.correctAnswer: As they have done unto this day
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:8 emphasizes continuing loyalty to God as they have done up to that point, highlighting faithfulness and obedience as essential for their continued success and relationship with God, linking with the warnings in verse 7.

questions.question: How does Joshua 23:9 describe the strength of the nations the LORD has driven out before Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Great nations and strong
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:9 states that the LORD drove out great and strong nations, yet no man was able to stand against Israel, underscoring God's power and faithfulness, which aligns with the encouragement in verses 7 and 8 to remain faithful.

questions.question: What promise is given in Joshua 23:10 regarding the strength Israel will have in battle?
options: One man of you shall chase a thousand
You will fight alone without help
You will need to hire mercenaries
You will only defeat small groups
questions.correctAnswer: One man of you shall chase a thousand
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:10 promises extraordinary victory for Israel, stating one man will chase a thousand because the LORD fights for them, which connects with the call to courage and faithfulness in preceding verses 8 and 9.

questions.question: According to Joshua 23:11, what must the Israelites take good heed to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Love the LORD their God
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:11 instructs the Israelites to take good heed to themselves to love the LORD their God, reinforcing the importance of faith and obedience given in earlier verses such as 7-10.

questions.question: What consequences does Joshua 23:12 warn will happen if the Israelites go back and cleave to the remnant of these nations and intermarry with them?
options: They will gain peace and prosperity
The LORD will no longer drive out these nations
They will be accepted by their gods
They will become rulers of other nations
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will no longer drive out these nations
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:12 warns that if Israel turns back and cleaves to the remaining nations and intermarry, the LORD will stop driving out those nations, leading to negative consequences as expanded in verse 13.

questions.question: What does Joshua 23:13 describe will happen to Israel if they fail to obey the LORD and intermarry with remaining nations?
options: They will become a great nation
They will be snares, traps, scourges, and thorns until they perish
They will be blessed with long life
They will gain control over all nations
questions.correctAnswer: They will be snares, traps, scourges, and thorns until they perish
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:13 shows the dire consequences of disobedience: the remaining nations will become snares and scourges, causing Israel to perish from the good land God gave them, reinforcing the warnings of verses 11 and 12.

questions.question: How does Joshua 23:14 assure the Israelites about the LORD's promises?
options: Some promises have failed, but most are kept
Not one thing has failed of all the good things the LORD promised
The promises depend on their future actions
The promises were only for Moses' generation
questions.correctAnswer: Not one thing has failed of all the good things the LORD promised
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:14 affirms that all the good promises of the LORD have come to pass without failure, encouraging trust and obedience, linking to the call to love and obey God in verses 11-13.

questions.question: What does Joshua 23:15 say will come upon Israel if they disobey the LORD as they have been blessed so far?
options: The LORD will bring upon them all evil things until destroyed from the good land
They will be protected from enemies
They will be forgiven without consequences
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will bring upon them all evil things until destroyed from the good land
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:15 warns that just as good things have come upon Israel for obedience, evil will come upon them for disobedience until they are destroyed from the land God gave them, reinforcing the covenant consequences described earlier.

questions.question: Based on Joshua 23:16, what triggers the anger of the LORD and leads to Israel's quick perishing from the land?
options: Transgressing the covenant and serving other gods
questions.correctAnswer: Transgressing the covenant and serving other gods
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:16 clearly states that breaking the covenant by serving and bowing to other gods will kindle the LORD's anger, causing Israel to perish quickly from the good land, which ties back to the admonitions found throughout the chapter.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 23:1 indicates that Joshua was young and vigorous when he called all Israel together.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:1 says Joshua was old and stricken in age when he assembled Israel, indicating his advanced years rather than youthfulness.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 23:6, the Israelites are instructed to be very courageous to keep and do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:6 commands courage in keeping and doing all the law of Moses, highlighting obedience as central to Israel's success, consistent with later warnings and promises.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 23:4 states that the land was divided among the tribes by Joshua without any reference to the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:4 says Joshua divided the land by lot as the LORD had cut off nations for them, attributing the division and conquest to God's work, not Joshua's independent action.

questions.question: What does Joshua 23:10 teach us about faith and trust in God in the context of battle?
options: The LORD fights for Israel, enabling one man to chase a thousand
Israel must train harder to win
All battles will be easy and without struggle
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD fights for Israel, enabling one man to chase a thousand
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:10 teaches that victory is from the LORD fighting for Israel, illustrating faith and trust in God's power over physical strength, supporting the theme of courage in verses 6-11.

questions.question: A fellow believer struggles with the temptation to intermarry with unbelievers. Based on Joshua 23, what biblical truth applies to this situation?
options: Intermarriage will bring peace and blessings
Intermarriage can cause Israel to lose God's protection and bring snares
Marriage choices are irrelevant to faithfulness
God does not care about whom one marries
questions.correctAnswer: Intermarriage can cause Israel to lose God's protection and bring snares
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:12-13 warns that intermarriage with remaining nations leads to loss of God's protection and results in snares and suffering, teaching the importance of faithfulness and obedience in personal relationships.

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 23 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 23.

questions.question: According to Joshua 23:13, what will happen if Israel cleaves to the remnant of the nations that remain among them?
options: They will be blessed with prosperity
They shall be snares, traps, scourges, and thorns until they perish
They will be given more land by the LORD
They will live peacefully with those nations
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be snares, traps, scourges, and thorns until they perish
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:13 states that if Israel cleaves to the remnant of these nations, they will become snares, traps, scourges, and thorns until they perish from the good land given by the LORD.

questions.question: What does Joshua say about the fulfillment of the LORD's promises in Joshua 23:14?
options: Only some promises have been fulfilled
Not one thing of all the good things has failed
The promises will be fulfilled in the future
questions.correctAnswer: Not one thing of all the good things has failed
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:14 affirms that every good thing the LORD promised has come to pass and not one has failed, underscoring God's faithfulness.

questions.question: What consequence does Joshua warn about in Joshua 23:15 if Israel disobeys the covenant?
options: They will experience all evil things until destroyed from the land
They will be exiled to Egypt
They will be given new laws
questions.correctAnswer: They will experience all evil things until destroyed from the land
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:15 warns that as all good things have come upon Israel, so will all evil things come upon them until they are destroyed from the good land if they disobey.

questions.question: According to Joshua 23:16, what causes the LORD's anger to be kindled against Israel?
options: Serving other gods and bowing to them
Building new altars to the LORD
Offering sacrifices to the LORD only
questions.correctAnswer: Serving other gods and bowing to them
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:16 states the LORD's anger is kindled when Israel transgresses the covenant by serving other gods and bowing to them.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the warning about serving other gods and the resulting judgment in Joshua 23:16?
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 28:15-68
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 28:15-68 contains blessings and curses linked to obedience and disobedience, echoing Joshua 23:16's warning about serving other gods and facing judgment.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Joshua 23:14-15 to contrast the outcomes of obedience and disobedience?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:14-15 uses chiasm by paralleling the fulfillment of good things with the coming of evil things, highlighting the consequences of obedience and disobedience.

questions.question: In Joshua 23:13, what metaphorical terms are used to describe the remaining nations among Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Snares, traps, scourges, and thorns
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:13 describes the remaining nations as snares, traps, scourges, and thorns, metaphorically emphasizing the danger they pose to Israel's faithfulness.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'cleave' in Joshua 23:8 and 23:12?
questions.correctAnswer: To join or cling firmly
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'דָּבַק' (dabaq), translated as 'cleave,' means to join or cling firmly, emphasizing Israel's need to remain steadfast to the LORD as in Joshua 23:8 and 23:12.

questions.question: Joshua 23:14 says 'I am going the way of all the earth.' What does this phrase most likely signify?
options: Joshua traveling to a new land
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua's impending death
questions.explanation: The phrase 'I am going the way of all the earth' in Joshua 23:14 is a euphemism for death, indicating Joshua's awareness of his mortality.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of faithfulness to God and warnings against idolatry similar to Joshua 23:7-8?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Corinthians 10:14-22
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 10:14-22 warns against idolatry and urges believers to remain faithful to God, echoing the warnings in Joshua 23:7-8.

questions.question: According to Joshua 23:10, what is the ratio of men Israel can chase due to the LORD fighting for them?
questions.correctAnswer: One man chases a thousand
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:10 states that one man of Israel shall chase a thousand because the LORD fights for them, emphasizing divine empowerment.

questions.question: What is the primary command Joshua gives to Israel in Joshua 23:6 to maintain their success?
options: To be courageous and obey all the law of Moses without turning right or left
To make alliances with surrounding nations
questions.correctAnswer: To be courageous and obey all the law of Moses without turning right or left
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:6 commands Israel to be very courageous and keep all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, without deviation.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book and chapter contain a similar exhortation to 'love the LORD your God' as found in Joshua 23:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 6
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6 contains the Shema, commanding Israel to love the LORD with all their heart, similar to Joshua 23:11's exhortation.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 23:9 emphasizes that no nation has been able to stand before Israel because of the LORD's intervention.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:9 states the LORD has driven out great nations and no man has been able to stand before Israel, confirming the truth of the statement.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 23:4 declares that the inheritance for the tribes is only on the east side of Jordan.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:4 says the inheritance is from Jordan to the great sea westward, not only on the east side, so the statement is false.

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 23 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 23 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by God in His promise to expel the nations before Israel and give them their land?
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:5 shows that the LORD will expel the nations and give their land as He promised, demonstrating His faithfulness in fulfilling His covenant promises.

questions.question: According to Joshua 23:6, what is the essential attitude Israel must maintain toward God's law?
questions.correctAnswer: Courageous obedience
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:6 commands Israel to be very courageous to keep and do all that is written in the law, emphasizing the necessity of bold and faithful obedience.

questions.question: What theological warning does Joshua give regarding intermarriage with the remaining nations in the land?
options: It will cause the LORD to stop driving out the nations and become a snare to Israel
It will lead to economic prosperity
It is permitted if the nations convert
questions.correctAnswer: It will cause the LORD to stop driving out the nations and become a snare to Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:12-13 warns that if Israel intermarry with the nations, the LORD will no longer drive them out and they will become traps and thorns until Israel perishes from the land.

questions.question: Which doctrine is most clearly reflected in Joshua's reminder that 'not one thing hath failed' of God's promises to Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of Divine Providence
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:14 affirms that all God’s promises have come to pass, illustrating divine providence—God’s sovereign and faithful governance over history.

questions.question: How does Joshua 23:10 characterize the power of God in battle for Israel?
options: The LORD fights for Israel, enabling one to chase a thousand
Victory depends on the number of soldiers
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD fights for Israel, enabling one to chase a thousand
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:10 declares that God fights for Israel, empowering them beyond natural ability, showing His sovereign power in their victories.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Joshua 23:7 and Joshua 23:16 provide about idolatry and covenant faithfulness?
options: Idolatry leads to the LORD’s anger and swift judgment
Idolatry is required for peace with neighbors
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry leads to the LORD’s anger and swift judgment
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:7 forbids serving other gods, and Joshua 23:16 warns that serving other gods will kindle the LORD’s anger and cause swift destruction, highlighting covenant faithfulness's essential nature.

questions.question: What does Joshua 23:4 reveal about the nature of God's distribution of land to Israel?
options: It was divided by lot as a sovereign act of God
It was purchased from the nations
It was assigned by Israel's own decision
questions.correctAnswer: It was divided by lot as a sovereign act of God
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:4 states that the land was divided by lot, indicating God's sovereign control and providence in distributing the inheritance.

questions.question: According to Joshua 23:9, what has been the outcome of the LORD's intervention on behalf of Israel?
options: No man has been able to stand before Israel
questions.correctAnswer: No man has been able to stand before Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:9 affirms that the LORD has driven out strong nations and that none has been able to withstand Israel, showing God's protective power.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about covenant blessings and curses is taught by combining Joshua 23:14 and Joshua 23:15?
options: God’s blessings and curses are conditional upon Israel’s obedience
Blessings are permanent but curses are temporary
Curses come regardless of Israel’s actions
questions.correctAnswer: God’s blessings and curses are conditional upon Israel’s obedience
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:14 confirms all blessings have come to pass as promised, while verse 15 warns of curses if Israel disobeys, teaching conditional covenant outcomes based on obedience.

questions.question: How does Joshua 23:11 emphasize the relationship between love for God and covenant faithfulness?
options: Love for God is unrelated to obedience
Loving the LORD is essential to keep His covenant
Love is optional in covenant faithfulness
Covenant faithfulness is based on fear, not love
questions.correctAnswer: Loving the LORD is essential to keep His covenant
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:11 exhorts Israel to love the LORD, indicating that covenant faithfulness is rooted in heartfelt love for God.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Joshua 23:1-2 establish in the grand story of redemption?
options: The end of Israel’s wilderness wanderings
Joshua’s final charge before the new generation inherits the land
The beginning of the monarchy in Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua’s final charge before the new generation inherits the land
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:1-2 depict Joshua, old and aged, giving his final exhortation to Israel, marking transition in the redemptive narrative from conquest to settlement.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about God’s justice and mercy is evident in Joshua 23:13 and Joshua 23:16?
options: God ignores sin among His people
God’s justice punishes covenant unfaithfulness, but His mercy provided the land
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice punishes covenant unfaithfulness, but His mercy provided the land
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:13 warns of punishment for covenant breach, while 23:16 reminds that God gave the good land, showing both His justice in judgment and mercy in provision.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that promises of divine help in battle are merely ancient myths. What does Joshua 23:9-10 actually teach about God’s involvement in Israel’s military victories?
options: God actively fights for Israel, ensuring their victory even against stronger foes
Israel wins only by their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: God actively fights for Israel, ensuring their victory even against stronger foes
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:9-10 states explicitly that the LORD has driven out strong nations and fights for Israel, empowering them beyond natural ability, showing active divine intervention.

questions.question: What theological meaning can be drawn from Joshua’s statement in 23:14 about 'going the way of all the earth'?
options: Human mortality contrasts with God’s eternal faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Human mortality contrasts with God’s eternal faithfulness
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:14 acknowledges his mortality but contrasts it with the unchanging fulfillment of God’s promises, emphasizing God’s eternal faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Joshua 23:8 instruct Israel to maintain their relationship with God in light of the conquest?
options: By cleaving to the LORD as they have done up to now
By adopting the customs of the remaining nations
questions.correctAnswer: By cleaving to the LORD as they have done up to now
questions.explanation: Joshua 23:8 commands Israel to continue cleaving to the LORD, maintaining covenant loyalty as they have done previously.
